title.value: IGLUE: A Benchmark for Transfer Learning across Modalities, Tasks, and Languages
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: IGLUE: A Benchmark for Transfer Learning across Modalities, Tasks, and Languages

extractions.description: The paper introduces IGLUE, a new benchmark designed to evaluate multilingual multimodal models for transfer learning. It focuses on tasks involving vision-and-language processing across 20 diverse languages. By combining tasks like visual question answering, cross-modal retrieval, visual reasoning, and entailment, IGLUE fills the gap in multilingual benchmarks in the vision-and-language domain. Researchers can now evaluate models in zero-shot and few-shot learning scenarios across languages and tasks.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on creating a benchmark for multilingual and multimodal transfer learning in vision-and-language tasks. It does not center around Climate Change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Reliable evaluation benchmarks designed for replicability and comprehensiveness have driven progress in machine learning. Due to the lack of a multilingual benchmark, however, vision-and-language research has mostly focused on English language tasks.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific Climate Change category as it primarily discusses methodologies for multilingual multimodal benchmarks.
primary_category.quote: IGLUE is the first evaluation suite for multilingual multitask V&L modelling, comprising five datasets across four structurally different tasks that require different levels of syntactic-semantic V&L understanding in cross-lingual setups.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not cover any secondary Climate Change themes as it is centered on computational methods for transfer learning benchmarks.
secondary_categories.quote: Aiming at a representative selection of languages, IGLUE covers 20 typologically diverse languages, spanning 11 lan-guage families, 9 scripts, and 3 WALS-defined geographical macro-areas.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category related to Climate Change is applicable given the paper's focus on multilingual vision-and-language benchmarks.
primary_sub_category.quote: We introduce the Image-Grounded Language Understanding Evaluation (IGLUE) benchmark. IGLUE brings together visual question answering, cross-modal retrieval, grounded reasoning, and grounded entailment tasks across 20 diverse languages.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not address any secondary sub-categories relevant to Climate Change.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our benchmark enables the evaluation of multilingual multimodal models for transfer learning, not only in a zero-shot setting, but also in newly defined few-shot learning setups.

applications.justification: There are no specific applications related to Climate Change discussed in this paper.
applications.quote: Based on the evaluation of the available state-of-the-art models, we find that translate-test transfer is superior to zero-shot transfer and that few-shot learning is hard to harness for many tasks.

new_primary_category.justification: No new climate change category is necessary as the paper does not relate to Climate Change.
new_primary_category.quote: Aiming to facilitate modelling and evaluation in multilingual vision-and-language research, IGLUE brings together 5 datasets across 4 structurally different tasks in 20 diverse languages.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: A new sub-category is unnecessary as the paper does not discuss topics directly related to Climate Change.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our benchmark aims to encourage future research efforts in this area by releasing the IGLUE benchmark to the community.
